EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  April 24, 2017

CALL TO ORDER

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling Hills
Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT

Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Carrie Silvano* Tim
Zingrang

*Member Silvano arrived at 7:08 p.m.

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT

Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2016

MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE NOVEMBER 28, 2016 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

Representatives from California Water Service provided information about the PV Peninsula
Water Reliability Project. Angie Gilbride, Regional Community Affairs Specialist, and Korey
Bradbury, Operations Manager, presented an overview of the need for the project, timeline, and
the sections of bridle trails which will be temporarily closed during the new pipeline’s installation.
They assured the Committee that they will work with the equestrian community and residents
along these trail sections to minimize impacts. The representatives answered a number of
 questions from Committee Members, gave their contact information, and provided a website
that will be regularly updated about the project: www.pvpwaterproject.com. Chairman Schmitz
thanked the California Water Service Company staff for their presentation to the Equestrian
Committee.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 24, 2017  1
EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN STREET CROSSING PROJECTS UPDATE

The Community Services Director reported that City Council reviewed a bid packet on April
11, 2017 and authorized staff to solicit bids. Bid results will be presented to City Council in May,
with work expected to begin on the Rolling Hills Road and Palos Verdes Drive North lighted
street crossings project in June.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

HOWLETT PARK JUDGES BOOTH PROJECT UPDATE

The Community Services Director reported that City Council approved Alan Pre-Fab Buildings
Corporation’s bid to build and deliver two custom horse show judges booths on March 28, 2017.
The Horse Show Judges Booth and Dressage Show Judges Booth are expected to be installed
by June 2017.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

2017 EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETINGS SCHEDULE

At the request of the CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ, the upcoming Equestrian Committee Meetings
schedule was distributed to Committee Members. An error was found for June, with the correct
date being Monday, June 26, 2017.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

CHANDLER PARK ARENA RULES ENFORCEMENT MEASURES

The Community Services Director reviewed current measures in place for the City’s public
arenas which include staff responses to issues, licensed Horse Trainers monitoring training
activities, City officials’ periodic approvals of new arena rules, occasional Horse Trainers
meetings, and the ability to revoke a Business License through procedures outlined in the
City’s Municipal Code. Staff reported that the City intended to hold an annual mandatory Horse
Trainers meeting each February, following the City’s January 31st deadline to purchase a Horse
Trainers Permit and Business License without a penalty fee.
 He also reported that the City’s Administrative Services Director was researching infrared and
daytime video cameras for all of the City’s parks which would record activities occurring in the
horse arenas, including violations by Horse Trainers, recreational riders, or those turning out
horses where not allowed in certain public arenas. Several Committee Members voiced their
support of the daytime video monitors as the solution to decreasing Horse Trainer rule
violations.

The Community Services Director reported a recent incident in the Chandler Park horse arena
that may have involved a visually impaired rider. Several Committee Members were aware of
a visually impaired licensed Horse Trainer who exercised other rider’s horses in this arena.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 24, 2017  2
The Committee requested that the issue of providing reasonable accommodation for disabled
riders in the City’s horse arenas be placed on the next agenda.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

2017 LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS

A list of the currently licensed Horse Trainers was distributed to Committee Members. The
Community Services Director indicated that the lists had been posted at the City’s public horse
arenas and noted that the list will likely be updated as more trainers purchase Licenses and
Permits throughout the year. He then read the names of licensed horse trainers who were in
Category 1 and not permitted to train in the public arenas.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW

A staff report outlining the current Horse Trainers Permit fee, Horse Shows and Clinics fees,
and Howlett Park barn stall rental fees was reviewed by the Community Services Director. In
response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiries, staff were not recommending fee increases as
there had not been any significant increases in facilities maintenance costs in the past few years
and that the last increase for most of the fees occurred in fiscal years 2010-11 and 2013-14.
Committee Members stated they recalled more recent fee changes and CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ
asked staff to research past equestrian fee change dates and bring back a staff report for the
May 22, 2017 Equestrian Committee meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ TABLED THE STAFF REPORT AND
PLACED THIS ITEM ON THE MAY 22, 2017 EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
AGENDA.
 PROPOSED ANNUAL EQUESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS AND ACTIVITIES REPORT

At the request of CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ, the Community Services Director developed a list of
potential measurable items which could be included in an annual report. He indicated that the
report could be presented on a calendar year or fiscal year basis and CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ
responded that she preferred it to be on a fiscal year basis. In response to the Community
Services Director’s inquiry, Committee Members concurred that only City events, facilities, and
maintenance activities should be compiled and other private equestrian facilities and
organization’s information should not be collected.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN SERVICES LICENSES AND PERMITS SUBCOMMITTEE

The Community Services Director asked for volunteers to serve on this Subcommittee, which

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 24, 2017  3

will address the other types of equestrian services occurring within the City on public facilities
and trails, such as farriers, horse haulers, horse exercisers, and many more. He indicated that
all of these services, if paid for, require a Business License and perhaps a Permit, similar to
Horse Trainer Permits issued to those who make a living using the City’s public facilities and
trails.

MEMBERS BRTIS, KEMP, and SILVANO volunteered to be on this Subcommittee to work with
staff in reviewing potential Business License and Permit fees for a variety of equestrian services
business activities occurring in the City and on public property.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ inquired whether the dog issues at #4 Goldring Place had been resolved.
MEMBER SILVANO reported that she had gone by this residence on the trail and that the dogs
spooked her and other rider’s horses. She indicated that the new home owners have since
installed a barrier to restrict their dogs from being able to reach the rear fence.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
   MEMBER HARIK reported erosion on the upper trail section of trail in the George F
  Canyon Nature Preserve.

B.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE – MAY 6, 2017

  CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ encouraged Committee Members to ride with the City Council
  and enjoy a delicious pancake breakfast on Saturday, May 6th. The Community Services
  Director reported that with Jim Moore’s upcoming departure from the City that the staff
  was having difficulty finding horses for City Council to ride.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  PORTABLE WATER STORAGE UNIT AND WATER TRUCK PURCHASE AND
  RENTAL COST INFORMATION

  MEMBER DEAN-PORTER provided the Community Services Director an alternative
  portable water storage unit which could be purchased, to be compared to the potential
  purchase or rental of a water truck for use in the Howlett Park horse arenas and is
  scheduled for the May 22, 2017 Committee meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 24, 2017  4
B.  ACCOMODATING HORSE ARENA USERS WITH DISABILITIES

  A discussion regarding use of the City’s public riding arenas by persons with disabilities
  will be on the May 22, 2017 Committee meeting.

C.  EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW

  The Community Services Director will verify the dates that each equestrian fee was last
  adjusted for the May 22, 2017 Committee meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

MEMBER KEMP moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:17 p.m.
 Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 24, 2017  5
